name: Mane 'n Tail shampoo

lead: Mane 'n Tail is a hair-care brand that began as a shampoo and conditioner for show horses and is now marketed for people as well. People use it hoping for longer, fuller, shinier hair.

The company's marketing talks about stronger hair that resists breakage, and its own site describes the idea that it spurs growth as an 'underground rumor'. Dermatology-style explainers say shampoos change how hair looks and breaks rather than how fast follicles grow, so length gains reported by users usually come from less breakage.

paras: It is used as an ordinary shampoo and conditioner in the shower, sometimes alternated with the user's regular products. The brand also sells leave-in treatments and styling aids.

Health-media coverage lists dryness, frizz, itching or rash (particularly with some ingredients such as benzalkonium chloride) and colour fading on dyed hair. The label notes some versions are intended for horses, and the brand makes a human line.

angle.text: Used as a shampoo and conditioner, it aims at hair that looks thicker and shinier and keeps its length through less breakage. Whether it speeds growth itself is the subject of the rumour.

lead: Mane 'n Tail is a hair and skin care brand owned by Straight Arrow Products and sold in versions for humans and for horses [1]. According to the company, it began on a New Jersey horse farm where the founder's parents developed a shampoo and conditioner for show horses; riders began using it on their own hair and word spread [2].

People use it hoping for thicker, shinier, longer hair. The company's own page calls the notion that it encourages hair growth an 'underground rumor' and focuses on claims of reduced breakage and repaired split ends [2]. It also gets passing mentions on bodybuilding forums such as T Nation [3].
infobox: Mass retail, drug stores, tack shops [2]

paras: The line includes shampoos, conditioners, an all-in-one product, leave-in treatments, styling aids and hand and nail treatments, sold in mass merchants, drug stores, salons and tack and feed stores [2]. Health-media summaries list keratin, avocado and sunflower oils, panthenol (a vitamin B5 derivative) and, in some products, zinc pyrithione among the ingredients [4].

The company says the product began as a show-horse formula that horse owners adopted for themselves [2]. The brand has sponsored NASCAR drivers from 1995, appeared in films including Blades of Glory, and was an in-kind sponsor of the 2011 film The Greatest Movie Ever Sold [1].

Healthline's explainer reports that no shampoo truly thickens hair, though products can make hair look thicker; it lists possible benefits such as shine and reduced oiliness, and notes that the traditional formula is not suited to colour-treated hair [4]. It lists dryness, frizz, itching or rash and colour loss among reported downsides [4].

lore.intro: Horse shampoo is mentioned in passing in fitness forums and widely as a hair-growth folk idea [2][3].

claims.claim: Horse shampoo makes human hair grow faster
